commits.headline: fix(port): hostgen reads a definition that a shared header declares otherwise, and a record defined in a cast
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
rac1-decomp's include/callees.h declares callees with void * parameters;
the port's hand C and the functional candidates define some of them with
typed pointers, so Clang refused whole units (fastfunc.c, sound.c) and
every function in them became a stub: the program stopped at
func_001F99B0 before its first frame. A definition now wins over a
one-line header declaration (dropped in the prepared copy, no line moves).

help_00203E98.c casts to an unnamed struct in func_L00_00205278; Clang's
JSON…

them with a function of its own (in level 12 the first hook of func_00230A90 is
the one that clears the draw callback lists, then the voice and particle
hooks). The port compiled the engine's one copy of func_00230A90, and the
pause code, against the stubs, so in a level's arrival cinematic nothing
cleared the lists: one draw callback was added a frame and, after 64 of them,
their quads ran past the display list…

commits.headline: fix(hostgen): a local vector or matrix starts on a quadword in its frame
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
A caller's float m[4][4] landed at a frame offset that was not a multiple of
16, and the callee (func_002153E8, which the game compiled to quadword loads)
copied it with movaps: a general protection fault that the crash handler
reported as an access at host address (nil) in level 4's func_L04_002BB7B0.
Arrays of whole quadwords of 32-bit elements are now aligned to 16 in the frame,
as the console's compiler placed them.

Verified: the new test fails without the change and passes with it;…

when it finds no checkout; a…

commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A player named one image for each game. On a first start the Games page now
asks once for the folder their PlayStation 2 games are in. The launcher looks
through it, two folders deep, and tells a disc by the boot program its
SYSTEM.CNF names (read from the image, so the file's name does not matter).
Every game found that can be played is set up without more questions, and the
set-up goes on to the levels by itself, so what is left is Play.
